**Interviewee:** Priya Anand, Lead Grader. **Held on:** 2026-10-11.

**Interviewer:** Thank you for meeting again. We will keep this short and focus on how quality is reviewed across the grading team.

**Priya Anand:** That is fine.

**Interviewer:** How do you audit quality across the team?

**Priya Anand:** We audit a sample every month. The purpose is to check whether grading is being applied consistently and to identify anything that may need closer review. Most of the team is steady.

**Interviewer:** When you review the sample, are you looking for broad patterns or individual differences?

**Priya Anand:** Both. We look at the overall pattern, but individual grading approaches can also stand out. If someone is consistently more or less demanding, that becomes visible through the sample.

**Interviewer:** Is any individual grader stricter than the rest?

**Priya Anand:** Yes, two people stand out. Tomas Brennan and Hannah Lowe grade much stricter than the rest of the team.

**Interviewer:** Is that a one-off observation, or has it appeared more generally in your review?

**Priya Anand:** It is a distinction that has appeared in the team’s grading. They are the two people who stand out in that respect.

**Interviewer:** How do urgent cases get prioritised?

**Priya Anand:** Urgent cases get flagged by the grader who reads them. That initial flag is what brings the case forward for attention.

**Interviewer:** Does the same quality review process apply to those cases?

**Priya Anand:** The cases are still subject to review. The urgent flag affects prioritisation, while the grading remains part of the quality process.

**Interviewer:** Is there anything else you want to clarify about differences between graders?

**Priya Anand:** Only that most of the team is steady. The notable difference is the stricter grading approach I have described.
